title: Wyatt Sharp and Jerry Lane, the riverboat captain and MCA price bids
summary: One long answer covers Wyatt Sharp's hotel trick, running a band on the boat against the captain's wishes, and how MCA bids undercut him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: W-Y-A-T-T-S-H-A-R-P. I didn't know him. He played with me at Suburban Gardens, and he was a very bright man. He managed by hook or crook, by leaving his clothes in his locker after Suburban Gardens, that he slept two nights in the Roosevelt and paid for one. Yeah, that's the truth. Because he was on the Donbusters, you see. He played with Pinky on the Donbusters. So he'd move in and leave a call for Donbusters, six o'clock, and he'd move out. Because most of his clothes and his tucks were in the locker at the nightclub. And how he did it, I don't know. He lived at the Roosevelt for 30 nights, slept there 30 nights and paid for 15. That's how smart he was. So he went up to Jackson, organized his own band, and he took two names and made one name out of it and called himself Jerry Lane. And I heard his band. And unfortunately for me, the night that I heard his band, we were both playing in the same place and I had a six piece Dixieland combination because I took all kinds of jobs, you know, for money. And I didn't. I don't think I sounded too good because I know he had, he had been great, but you can't carry a whole band on your shoulders, you know. That's why when I got a good man, I kept him. And my dad said to me, never break up a winning combination. Many times I want to change. He says, is the boy doing a good job? I said, good. Don't break up a winning combination. And I always tried to be nice, I gave a good job, played plenty of music. I always let them know the tune I was playing too. Don't forget that. Like Louis says, I like to hear the tune I'm playing. I had to impress on me about arrangements because I used to have a lot of arrangements, good arrangements, but the way the music used to come out, you wouldn't have time. So I'd take the stocks and I'd trick them up. And other band leaders thought I was playing special. Because they used to come on the boat when I played on the boat. I played on the president. It was one series of arguments between the captain and I. I said to him one night, I said, Captain Stratfuss, I said, I honor you and I respect you. But why don't you run the band and let me run the boat? Which captain was this? Captain Stratfuss, Captain Roy, the old man. He'd keep handing me programs from St. Louis. I said, we are playing in New Orleans. We're not playing in St. Louis. I don't want to know what they're playing in St. Louis. I'm playing and I don't change my style for a month on the boat. I said, he says, well, they do say you give good, honest music. I said, no one has to tell me that I know it. And I said, your advisors, one of them particularly, couldn't get past the first inning when he tried to play with me. Couldn't even tell a chapter about me, I'd throw them overboard. Then he said, the same guy, and you mentioned his name a while ago. He's my friend now, we're friends, because he helped me collect a collection of Armstrong records. It was priceless. My little, my granddaughter knocked it off her table and ruined most of them. I almost died. I'm so hard. But Dutch Andrews helped me get the collection. But Dutch, well in order to strengthen himself, he'd give advice. Who was he to give advice? So I said, Captain, you run the band. I'll run the boat. We're both right up on the rocks. He wouldn't let me play at V&E's walls. I said, Captain, I cater through the years to different people, different clientele than you have. Not that I'm a snob, but I play for the richest. I play for carnival balls, supper dances, conventions. Why was I the number one band for MCA here for years? Why did, I didn't have to bid on jobs. Why did they say, are you available? And when I send the prices, he said, Johnny, we can't make any money with you. I said, why? You don't charge. He said, you don't charge enough. For instance, I remember years ago, it impressed me so that people, people like to get robbed. I bid on a Coca-Cola, imagine that the Edwards, that's another place. I can show you a letter with the man, you think I was just stunned, how he praises me. I bid $350 for Coca-Cola, and MCA gets me on the phone, Johnny, can you play Coca-Cola? I said, yes. I said, but I already bid on them. What did you bid? I said, $350. He said, no good. I said, how much? He said, $900. I ride back a variable, $900 in my car. Now how do you like that? For people like that. And the same man didn't even remember me. I said, I'm not going to buy a car. He didn't even remember me. He must have thrown my letter. You see the edgewater-
